messages:
Ira: Ran an nsys capture against the regression from commit abc123. Timeline shows matmul kernels being launched after KV prefetch ranges finish, causing a 3-4ms stall per request. Perfetto link: https://perfetto.local/abc123 (internal). Our current NVTX labels are just 'kv-prefetch' and 'kv-lookup' without request context, so hard to correlate to a specific request or kernel launch.

Alex: Got it. Are we running continuous batching for that run? If so the kernel selector might be choosing a slower path due to sequence length rounding. Also curious if the prefetch is on a separate CUDA stream that's forcing sync back to the main stream.

Maria: I pulled the trace — the critical section looks like:
kv_lookup -> kv_prefetch -> kernel:matmul_q4 -> idle -> kv_commit. The idle gap coincides with host->device memcpy on a different stream, so likely implicit sync. Screenshot: (attached).

Sam: @Ira can you paste the exact nsys command and the NVTX push we used? We should standardize naming so we can grep/filter in perfetto/nvidia tools.

Ira: nsys command I used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx -o /tmp/trace_abc123 --capture-range=nvtx --sample=nvtx --force-overwrite true --output=null`
And the NVTX push in the runtime looked like: 
```
char buf[256];
snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "kv-prefetch:%s", req_id);
nvtxRangePushA(buf);
// do prefetch
nvtxRangePop();
```
So it's a full string per op.

Maria: Two quick things: 1) avoid very long strings per push (makes the UI noisy), 2) we need a per-request outer span so all child ranges can be grouped in perfetto. Right now we only tag ops, no outer request span.

perf-bot: :bell: Automated note: perf monitoring flagged a 2.8% p50 latency regression for small-seq_len workloads on 2026-03-11 relative to yesterday. Trace ID: perf-20260311-08.

Alex: Proposal for NVTX naming: use a compact convention to make filtering easy and keep labels short. Example: outer span `r:<rid>` (contains attributes), then children: `kv:l` (lookup), `kv:p` (prefetch), `ks` (kernel_select), `kl:<kname>` (kernel_launch). Also attach nvtx marks/annotations for `seq_len` and `cache_hit` where helpful.

Ira: I like that. Also we should use `nvtxRangePushEx` with category bits (e.g., 0x1=KV, 0x2=Kernel, 0x4=IO) so perfetto can color/group quickly. Example: `nvtxRangePushEx(&params)` with `params.category = 0x1`.

Sam: Another practical point: do not push for every micro-op in hot loops; instead keep coarse ranges and mark micro-events with `nvtxMarkA` (lightweight). Otherwise NVTX overhead will perturb the profile.

Maria: I'll draft a patch:
- Add `r:<rid>` outer span at request entry (if REDWOOD_NVTX=1).
- Push child ranges: `kv:l`, `kv:p`, `ks`, `kl:<shortname>`; keep names <= 32 chars.
- Add `nvtxMarkA` inside tight loops for counters (cache_hit=1).
- Use category bits as Ira suggested.
I'll include an example `nsys` + perfetto query:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx -o /tmp/run --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none
# open in perfetto and filter: "slice.name CONTAINS 'r:'" then group by category
```

Ira: Questions for rollout: make opt-in via env REDWOOD_NVTX=1 and a feature flag that samples ~1% of requests by default. Also have a debug build where we can enable full tracing. Note: NVTX itself adds overhead — limit to request-level tracing in prod.

Alex: ACK. I'll add a sampling toggle in the telemetry layer (sample by hash(req_id) % 100 < SAMPLE_RATE). Default SAMPLE_RATE=1.

perf-bot: :white_check_mark: Remind: add a regression test that runs a short perfetto/nvtx smoke trace in CI (non-flaky) so NVTX changes don't accidentally bloat hot paths.

Maria: I'll open the PR later today with instrumentation + docs and a small test. Will tag @Alex and @Ira for review.

Ira: Thanks all. After the PR lands let's re-run the same nsys capture and confirm the kernel launch ordering and whether prefetch stayed async. If we still see idle gaps we'll dig into stream assignment in the kernel selector. :mag:
